nature.line: The first book given by God to the rational beings, is the nature of the created things. Written teachings have been added only after aberration.

body.line: The knowledge of God does not dwell in a body that loves comfort.

mystery.line: By faith we are instructed about those unattainable things, not by investigation and the power of knowledge.

effort.line: For the help of God is necessary for deliverance. When he knows that he needs divine help, he will frequently pray. And by much beseeching the heart becomes humble.

all.line: The retribution of the sinners is this, that He repays them with resurrection instead of with justice.

macrina.name: Macrina the Younger
macrina.dates: c. 327 to 379 (died 19 July 379, months after Basil)
macrina.hook: When her fiancé died she refused every other suitor, saying there is one marriage as there is one birth and one death; then she talked her proud brother Basil out of his rhetoric and her wealthy mother into sharing the servants' bread and beds.

learning.work: On the Soul and the Resurrection
learning.by: as her brother Gregory recorded her words

anger.work: On the Soul and the Resurrection
anger.line: But, whenever their impulse is towards what is noble, then they become matter for praise, as his desire did to Daniel, and his anger to Phineas, and their grief to those who nobly mourn.
anger.by: as her brother Gregory recorded her words

tell.line: Will you not cease to be insensible to the divine blessings? Will you not remedy the ingratitude of your soul?
tell.by: as her brother Gregory remembered it

tears.work: On the Soul and the Resurrection
tears.line: She quoted the Apostle's words about the duty of not being grieved for them that sleep; because only men without hope have such feelings.
tears.by: as her brother Gregory tells it

calm.work: On the Soul and the Resurrection
calm.line: It will therefore be no detriment to our participation in the Good, that the soul should be free from such emotions.
calm.by: as her brother Gregory recorded her words

mystery.work: On the Soul and the Resurrection
mystery.by: as her brother Gregory recorded her words

deeper.work: On the Soul and the Resurrection
deeper.line: It is impossible to make the framework of the narrative correspond with the truth, if we understand it literally; we can do that only by translating each detail into an equivalent in the world of ideas.
deeper.by: as her brother Gregory recorded her words

all.work: On the Soul and the Resurrection
all.line: But He that becomes all things will be in all things too; and herein it appears to me that Scripture teaches the complete annihilation of evil.
all.by: as her brother Gregory recorded her words

justin.name: Justin Martyr
justin.dates: c. 100 - c. 165 (beheaded at Rome under the prefect Junius Rusticus)
justin.hook: He shopped for a philosophy, walked out on a teacher who asked for his fee up front, met a stranger by the sea who talked him into Christ, and ended up beheaded in Rome after publicly humiliating a Cynic in debate.

learning.line: Whatever things were rightly said among all men, are the property of us Christians.

dreams.line: For the prophetical gifts remain with us, even to the present time.

miracles.line: For numberless demoniacs throughout the whole world, and in your city, many of our Christian men exorcising them in the name of Jesus Christ, Who was crucified under Pontius Pilate, have healed and do heal.

mystery.line: Philosophy is, in fact, the greatest possession, and most honourable before God, to Whom it leads us and alone commends us.

war.line: We who formerly used to murder one another do not only now refrain from making war upon our enemies.

irenaeus.name: Irenaeus of Lyons
irenaeus.hook: To mock a sect's grand names for the hidden powers of the universe, he coined his own: "a power which I term a Gourd", with "Utter-Emptiness", "the Cucumber" and "a Melon".

rich.line: For whatsoever we acquired from unrighteousness when we were heathen, we are proved righteous, when we have become believers, by applying it to the Lord's advantage.

body.line: Here he manifestly declares the body to be the temple in which the Spirit dwells.

dreams.line: Others have foreknowledge of things to come: they see visions, and utter prophetic expressions.

miracles.line: Others still, heal the sick by laying their hands upon them, and they are made whole.

mystery.line: We are able by the grace of God to explain some of them, while we must leave others in the hands of God.

all.line: Thus also the punishment of those who do not believe the Word of God, and despise His advent, and are turned away backwards, is increased; being not merely temporal, but rendered also eternal.

martin.name: Martin of Tours
martin.dates: born c. 316 (some scholars say c. 336) at Savaria in Pannonia (Szombathely, Hungary); bishop of Tours from c. 371; died 8 November 397 at Candes
martin.hook: A young cavalry guard cut his army cloak in half with his sword for a freezing beggar at Amiens, and later told the emperor on the eve of battle, "I am the soldier of Christ: it is not lawful for me to fight."

laugh.line: No one ever saw him enraged, or excited, or lamenting, or laughing.
laugh.by: as Sulpicius Severus, who knew him, recorded it

alone.line: Martin was accustomed to say to you, that such an abundance of power was by no means granted him while he was a bishop, as he remembered to have possessed before he obtained that office.
alone.by: as Sulpicius Severus, who knew him, recorded it

tell.by: as Sulpicius Severus, who knew him, recorded it

calm.line: No one ever saw him enraged, or excited, or lamenting, or laughing; he was always one and the same: displaying a kind of heavenly happiness in his countenance, he seemed to have passed the ordinary limits of human nature.
calm.by: as Sulpicius Severus, who knew him, recorded it

body.line: It is not fitting that a Christian should die except among ashes; and I have sinned if I leave you a different example.
body.by: as Sulpicius Severus, who knew him, recorded it

dreams.by: as Sulpicius Severus, who knew him, recorded it

miracles.by: as Sulpicius Severus, who knew him, recorded it

pure.by: as Sulpicius Severus, who knew him, recorded it

war.line: I am the soldier of Christ: it is not lawful for me to fight.
war.by: as Sulpicius Severus, who knew him, recorded it

rulers.by: as Sulpicius Severus, who knew him, recorded it

benedict.name: Benedict of Nursia
benedict.dates: c. 480 - c. 547 (traditional dates; the only early source gives no years)
benedict.hook: He walked out of the schools of Rome as a young man, lived three years in a cave where a friend lowered bread to him on a rope with a little bell tied to it, and later wrote a Rule so down to earth that it lets monks drink wine because, it admits, they cannot be persuaded to give it up.

laugh.line: But as for buffoonery or idle words, such as move to laughter, we utterly condemn them in every place, nor do we allow the disciple to open his mouth in such discourse.

quiet.line: The ninth degree of humility is that a monk restrain his tongue from speaking; and, keeping silence, do not speak until he is spoken to.

learning.by: as Gregory the Great recorded it

tell.line: Let him not shut his eyes to the faults of offenders; but as soon as they appear, let him strive with all his might to root them out.

effort.line: If he sees some good in himself, let him credit it to God, not to himself. But let him know that evil is always his own doing, and count it as his own.

boethius.name: Boethius
boethius.hook: The most powerful civil servant in Gothic Italy was condemned without a hearing, and in his cell awaiting a brutal death he wrote a book in which Philosophy walks in and throws out the Muses of self-pity.

learning.line: Examine carefully what I have said, and if possible, reconcile faith and reason.

anger.line: Pity is rather due to the criminal, who ought to be brought to the judgment-seat by his accusers in a spirit not of anger, but of compassion and kindness.

calm.line: Joy, hope and fear Suffer not near, Drive grief away: Shackled and blind And lost is the mind Where these have sway.

mystery.line: I have long pondered this problem with such mind as I have and all the light that God has lent me.

effort.line: Therefore, withstand vice, practise virtue, lift up your souls to right hopes, offer humble prayers to Heaven.
